content: You help people edit Power BI paginated reports (.rdl files) using the pbirb tools. Tools are available for data sources, datasets and queries, parameters, tables and matrices, text and cell styling, page layout, headers and footers, charts, images, and actions. The user's message names the report file. Make the requested change directly without asking for confirmation, and keep the rest of the report intact. If the tools cannot do what is asked, say so plainly instead of improvising.

Report file: /var/folders/zl/zqyf2h6n3md3dcg8g9cdfm380000gp/T/pbirb-eval-d08-1d5_bxtv/report.rdl

Nothing uses FuelLitres any more. Remove that field from the dataset.

The FuelLitres field is also a `SUM` column in the DAX query, so I'll remove the field and the query column together so they stay in sync. Checking for references first.
The positional remap changed the data-bound columns in a way I didn't intend. Checking the current field mapping.

The remap pointed `OperatingHours` and `IdleHours` at the `Usage` table and pointed `Utilization` at `ScheduledHours`, which is wrong. I'll restore those three fields to their original `[Name]` column references. The field definitions are re-added immediately, so the report's expressions are unaffected.

I removed the FuelLitres field from DataSet1 and took its column out of the DAX query, so the query and field list still line up.

The DAX query now has no `FuelLitres` column. The dataset fields are AssetID, AssetName, Site, EquipmentType, ReportDate, OperatingHours, IdleHours and Utilization. Nothing else in the report was changed.

One side effect to know about: the query-column remap briefly pointed the OperatingHours, IdleHours and Utilization fields at the wrong source columns. I restored them to their original `[OperatingHours]`, `[IdleHours]` and `[Utilization]` mappings and checked the result. Those three fields now sit at the end of the field list, not in their original position. That shouldn't affect anything, since fields are matched by name.

I didn't open the report in Report Builder or run the query, so it's worth a quick preview to confirm the data still renders.
